Historical Commission meeting minutes, November 18, 2026 
Page 1 of 4 
 
 
DRAFT 
SALEM HISTORICAL COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
November 18, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Historical Commission was held on November 18, 2026, at 6:00 PM via Zoom 
Virtual Meeting.  Present were Milo Martinez, Robert Peterson, Chair Kelly Tyler-Lewis, Vice Chair 
Rebecca English, Mark Meche, and Margarida Raka-Goncalves.  Staff: Patti Kelleher. Absent: Vijay 
Joyce, Emily Gonzalez, Brendan Murray. 
 
348 Essex Street 
Andrea Bennett applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace three-tab asphalt roof shingles with 
architectural roof shingles. 
 
This application was reviewed as a minor change under the Historical Commission policy for architectural 
roof shingles.  No objection was received, and a Certificate was issued on October 26, 2026. 
 
9 Lynn Street 
Timothey and Margaret Doggett applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for architectural roof 
shingles. 
 
This application was reviewed as a minor change under the Historical Commission policy for architectural 
roof shingles.  No abutter objection was received, and a Certificate was issued on November 6, 2026. 
 
396 Essex Street–continuation 
Daniel Levitt applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for door modifications. 
 
Mr. Levitt reported that a site visit had taken place since the prior meeting.  Following recommendations 
from the Commission, he had contacted Joe Valone of Second Life, Jeff Grinaml, and Bach Woodcraft 
for repair estimates.  One or more estimates approached $10,000, which the applicant considered high.  
He discussed possible interim use of plywood, sanding and repairing deteriorated portions of the door 
with wood epoxy, and the possibility of installing kick plates. 
 
Mr. Meche favored stabilizing and preserving the existing historic veneer and finish rather than replacing 
substantial portions of the door.  He discussed lightweight repair products, polyurethane or an oil-based 
clear finish, and a boat varnish mentioned in one estimate.  He advised against removing the molding and 
observed that some evidence of age was part of the door’s history.  Chair Tyler-Lewis stated that 
deteriorated veneer and trim would need to be repaired or replaced as appropriate.  Members discussed a 
durable repair that would arrest deterioration while retaining the door’s appearance. 
 
Public comment:  
Jeff Bellin and Laura Wiseman, fellow owners, sought clarification about the repair estimates and whether 
the Commission recommended replacing the door’s veneer or outer skin, described as approximately one-
quarter inch thick.  Mr. Meche clarified that his preference was to stabilize and retain as much material as 
possible.  Ms. Wiseman requested definite guidance.  Chair Tyler-Lewis explained that the Commission
Historical Commission meeting minutes, November 18, 2026 
Page 2 of 4 
 
 
could evaluate preservation approaches but could not diagnose the underlying condition or prescribe a 
particular repair.  Mr. Bellin expressed concern that buckling and cracks allowed water infiltration.  Ms. 
Wiseman asked whether the existing door was made of Cuban mahogany. 
 
Mr. Meche favored allowing time to consult with the applicant’s preferred repair professional and 
volunteered to review the work on behalf of the Commission.  Ms. Kelleher explained that an in-kind 
repair without changes could qualify for a Certificate of Non-Applicability.  Mr. Levitt indicated that kick 
plates were no longer desired.  Members favored stabilizing the door while retaining its historic fabric.  
Ms. Kelleher also referenced recent door-restoration proposals at City Hall and Dickson Chapel. 
 
No vote was taken.  The discussion concluded with the understanding that the proposed in-kind repair 
would proceed through the Certificate of Non-Applicability process. 
 
6 Manning Street 
Beth Anne and Matthew Cornell applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish more than 50 
percent of the façade of a building older than 50 years. 
 
Michael Proscia of Jones Architecture was present.  Mr. Proscia presented existing and proposed views of 
the detached garage at the rear of the property, which would be converted to a detached accessory 
dwelling unit.  The existing footprint would remain substantially unchanged, but portions of all four 
exterior walls would be altered, with more than half of at least two façades proposed for demolition.  The 
aluminum siding and garage door would be removed, new windows and doors would be installed except 
on the property-line side, and the reconstructed building would have fiber-cement siding. 
 
Mr. Proscia stated that the house dated to approximately 1926 and the garage to approximately 1927 or 
later.  To his knowledge, the property was not in an historic district and had no MACRIS record. Ms. 
Kelleher confirmed that the garage was not inventoried.  In response to Mr. Meche’s question about 
framing, Mr. Proscia described larger, rough-cut two-by-four lumber from the 1920s.  Members expressed 
the opinion that the garage was not historically significant. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. Raka-Goncalves motioned to find the garage not historically significant.  Ms. English 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Martinez, English, Peterson, Meche, Raka-Goncalves, Tyler-Lewis were 
in favor, and the motion so carried. 
 
107 Federal Street–continuation 
Susan Hacker applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for an air-conditioning condenser and exterior 
electrical work after the fact. 
 
Ms. Kelleher displayed a photographic mockup of an enclosure around the condensers.  Ms. Hacker 
explained that the proposed approximately eight-foot-high enclosure would have shutter-style doors 
across its front, facing the parking area, to screen both condensers while allowing access.  The enclosure 
would be painted to match the building.  Chair Tyler-Lewis asked whether the elevated condenser could 
be relocated beside the ground-mounted unit. Ms. Hacker said that the nearby door and electrical meters 
presented placement difficulties.
Historical Commission meeting minutes, November 18, 2026 
Page 3 of 4 
 
 
Members discussed how to screen the electrical meters and condensers while retaining access and 
avoiding excessive encroachment into the parking area.  Mr. Meche discussed code-compliant approaches 
to painting or enclosing the meters.  Mr. Martinez asked about the existing three-sided fence and its 
access door, suggested louvers might not be necessary, and considered whether a single enclosure could 
accommodate the equipment.  Chair Tyler-Lewis preferred screening approximately six feet high or lower 
and recommended a site visit to assess the installation in relation to the parking lot. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to continue the application to the next meeting on November 18 to 
conduct a site visit.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Martinez, English, Peterson, 
Meche, Raka-Goncalves, Tyler-Lewis were in favor, and the motion so carried. 
 
7 Carpenter Street 
Patricia McCosco applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace a condenser.   
 
The applicant was not present. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the application to the next meeting on November 18.  Mr. 
Meche seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Martinez, English, Peterson, Meche, Raka-Goncalves, Tyler-
Lewis were in favor, and the motion so carried. 
 
21 Warren Street 
Carrie and Lee Dichter applied for a Certificate of Hardship for chimney removal.  
 
Chair Tyler-Lewis recused herself from discussion.  
 
The applicants were not present. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to continue the application to the next meeting on November 18.  Mr. 
Peterson seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Martinez, English, Peterson, Meche, Raka-Goncalves were in 
favor, and the motion so carried. 
 
 
145 Boston Street 
Juniper Point Investment Company LLC applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish a 
building older than 50 years. 
 
Dan Ricciarelli of Seger Architects was present.  Mr. Ricciarelli described the building as a small one-
story Cape with a two-story addition.  Photographs were displayed.  Ms. Kelleher discussed an inventory 
form that assigned a ca. 1940 construction date based on visual analysis.  She also reported that an 1897 
atlas depicted a square building on the lot.  Mr. Ricciarelli stated his believe that the existing building 
replaced an earlier structure.  The discussion referenced ownership by George Gartland between 
approximately 1930 and 1941, followed by a sale to John O’Connor.
Historical Commission meeting minutes, November 18, 2026 
Page 4 of 4 
 
 
Mr. Ricciarelli said the applicant was considering design options but had no immediate reconstruction 
plan.  Property owner Marc Trainos was present on the call and said he believed the chimney led to a 
fireplace and that he hoped to build something more in keeping with the neighborhood.  Ms. Kelleher 
observed that the application proposed complete demolition, although the relevant demolition threshold 
could also be reached through partial removal of a building or roof.  She expressed concern that the 
existing structure could be older than estimated, given the chimney.  Members favored a site visit before 
making a determination. 
 
Public comment:  
Tina and Martin Noone, owners of neighboring 147 Boston Street, expressed concern about construction 
noise and debris if the building were demolished. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to continue the application to the next meeting on November 18 to 
conduct a site visit.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Martinez, English, Peterson, 
Meche, Raka-Goncalves, Tyler-Lewis were in favor, and the motion so carried. 
 
33 Walter Street 
Juniper Point Investment Company LLC applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish a 
building older than 50 years.   
 
The applicant requested a withdrawal without prejudice. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to accept the request to withdraw without prejudice.  Mr. Peterson 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Martinez, English, Peterson, Meche, Raka-Goncalves, Tyler-Lewis were 
in favor, and the motion so carried. 
 
 
 
Other Business 
11 Cambridge Street 
The Commission discussed a proposal to reconstruct a rear deck and a portion of a covered porch visible 
from the street.  A new composite material, identified as ACRE, was proposed.  The project carpenter 
reportedly indicated that it could be cut to match existing decorative trim and balusters.  Members 
discussed scheduling a site visit, and Chair Tyler-Lewis requested a sample of the milled material. 
 
 
Adjournment 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to adjourn.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  All were in favor, and the 
motion so carried. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:48 PM. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Dan Graham, Historical Commission Clerk
